what: The whole panel flows as a WebGL color field — a value-noise fbm warped twice (domain warp) drifts slowly in stripes stretched along one axis (vertical·horizontal), five color layers overlap at each threshold, faint lines rise on some layer boundaries, and 12fps grain flickers. Only near the cursor (Gaussian radius .15) is the pattern pushed and rippling (.1, the cursor follows by .04 per frame), on open the color field spreads out of a single color over 1.15s with (1−(1−t)^2.2), and when settle is given, contours tighten by (progress/settle)² until scroll reaches that share, gathering into the single color c1

options.scale: Pattern size (larger is finer), default 3.5 — contact is 3.2
options.streak: How much it stretches into stripes, default 3.5 — 6 for contact
options.angle: Stripe axis (deg), 0 is vertical lines · 90 is horizontal lines (contact)
options.push: Strength of the cursor pushing the pattern, default .1 · 0 means no cursor reaction
options.soft: Half-width of the blur at layer boundaries, default .025 — contact is .1125
options.cover: Share at which the border appears (0~1), default .3 — .5 for contact
options.top: Height of the band fading out from the top by --fx-top (0~1), default .9 · none if 0
options.settle: When scroll progress (0~1) reaches this share, everything gathers into the single c1 color, default .5 · 0 means no gathering
options.--fx-c0 ~ --fx-c4 · --fx-line · --fx-top: (css variables) colors, borders and top band for five layers — by default made from --kf-accent, --kf-accent-soft and --kf-bg

from.where: about.html .am-field (vertical-line blue and pink color fields, solid blue at half scroll) · contact.html .am-field (horizontal-line dark navy color field — angle: 90; streak: 6; scale: 3.2; octaves: 4; contrast: 1.1; soft: .1125; cover: .5; top: 0; settle: 0)

note: The original uses a screen-fixed canvas with a window-based cursor — the part measures from the size and position of the element it is attached to, so to use it as a screen background make the element position: fixed; inset: 0 stays. The shader compiles right when attached (so it doesn’t stall on the first cursor move).
